title: Career roadmap · Cargo Executive
summary: Build expertise in air-cargo operations, documentation, warehouse processes, dangerous-goods awareness, customs procedures, cargo technology, and airport coordination to enter airline, airport, cargo-terminal, freight-forwarding, and logistics operations.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a 3-year B.Sc route beginning in 2026. For a 4-year honours route, use the additional year for advanced cargo operations, dangerous-goods training, airport internships, logistics analytics, and a substantial industry project.

about.label: Course alignment
about.text: Cargo Executive is directly aligned with Aviation (Hons) / Airport Ground Handling.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build airport operations, air-cargo, documentation, warehouse, customer-service and safety knowledge; target Cargo Operations Intern / Ground Handling Intern / Cargo Assistant / Airport Operations Trainee.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop expertise in cargo documentation, ULD operations, warehouse systems, customs coordination, freight forwarding and cargo-management software; target Cargo Executive / Cargo Operations Executive / Air Freight Executive.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Move toward cargo planning, key-account management, export/import coordination, cargo compliance or supervisory operations.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine aviation expertise with cargo analytics, automation, digital documentation, supply-chain technology, sustainability and risk management.

items: Cargo Operations Intern / Ground Handling Intern — 0–2 years
Cargo Executive / Air Freight Executive — 1–4 years
Senior Cargo Executive / Cargo Coordinator — 3–7 years
Cargo Operations Supervisor / Cargo Planning Specialist — 6–10 years
Cargo Operations Manager / Air Freight Manager — 8–14 years
Airport Cargo Manager / Regional Cargo Manager — 12+ years
Head of Cargo / Cargo Operations Director — 15+ years

blocks.text: Actual progression depends on employer, airport, cargo segment and professional qualifications.
A PhD is mainly useful for research, academia, advanced transport planning, policy or specialised analytics rather than ordinary Cargo Executive roles.

The long-term opportunity is to move from transaction-level cargo documentation into cargo network management, digital logistics, automation, analytics, compliance and strategic air-freight planning. Professionals who understand both airport operations and supply-chain technology should remain better positioned as air-cargo systems become increasingly digital.
